report.answer: An orange basketball is dropped and falls straight down in free-fall, then sticks the landing with no bounce. The fall fits a vertical projectile with Earth gravity, and after frame ~40 the ball is motionless on the floor — a completely dead, inelastic impact. Overlay shows the fitted gravity curve matching the measured centres to ~1.5 mm.
assumptions: fall is vertical in a plane facing the camera
scale from ball itself: 0.24 m +-0.01 m diameter at same depth as motion

forks.label: Drop this on the Moon
forks.why: Same drop with 1.62 m/s2 takes ~2.5x longer to fall

forks.label: Make it bouncy
forks.why: See a real basketball bounce sequence instead of a dead stop

forks.label: Remove air
forks.why: Drag was undetectable here; vacuum makes no visible change, confirming gravity dominates
